issues.legal_issue: A property appeal involving disputed tenant-protection claims may be disposed of through an equitable arrangement reflecting the parties’ proposed terms without deciding the underlying statutory entitlement.
material_facts: The tenants had leased a property comprising a small building and a large vacant area, and had erected structures for their mills on the vacant area.

The landlords disputed the tenants’ account of the lease and their entitlement to statutory protection; the lower courts had dismissed the tenants’ purchase application while granting limited protection against interference with possession.
The Supreme Court expressed doubts about the lower courts’ view of the lease, but the parties proposed an arrangement and left the Court to refine its terms.

The landlords agreed to bear the cost of shifting the tenants’ structures and to provide access to the area allotted to the tenants; the tenants agreed to compensate the landlords for the area allotted to them.
issues.conclusion: The appeal was disposed of on equitable terms: the tenants were to return the landlords’ building, the landlords were to receive a specified area and provide access, and the remaining area was allotted to the tenants subject to payment. The arrangement also provided for shifting the tenants’ structures and demarcating the areas. If the tenants failed to deposit the required consideration, the appeal would stand dismissed and the High Court’s order would remain in force.
issues.legal_principle: The Court did not decide the disputed entitlement under the Tamil Nadu City Tenants’ Protection Act, 1921, or rely on any earlier case as the basis for its disposition. It resolved the appeal through a case-specific equitable arrangement shaped by the parties’ proposals and concessions; the Act’s Sections 3 and 9 were part of the dispute below but were not applied to determine the appeal.

rule.if: property_appeal_pending and parties_leave_equitable_terms_to_court and (parties_offer_mutual_concessions and property_can_be_rearranged)

predicates.property_appeal_pending: An appeal is pending in a property dispute involving possession or allocation of leased property.
predicates.parties_leave_equitable_terms_to_court: The parties present proposed settlement terms and leave the Court to refine an equitable arrangement.
predicates.parties_offer_mutual_concessions: The opposing sides agree to concessions that facilitate a division or transfer of property and address its practical consequences.
predicates.property_can_be_rearranged: The property and structures can be rearranged or shifted so that the proposed allocation can be carried out.

issues.definition: When a property appeal is pending, the parties entrust proposed equitable terms to the Court, and mutual concessions and practical rearrangement make an allocation feasible, the appeal is disposed of on equitable terms.
